videos.title: How Is Bread Made? (Sliced Bread Was Once Banned) 🍞
videos.description:
In 1943 the US banned sliced bread to save steel during the war, and the ban lasted two months. Bread is flour, water, yeast and salt: kneading builds stretchy gluten, yeast makes gas that the gluten traps, and the oven turns the outside into a crust. Sliced bread has been sold since 1928.
Crust: eat it or leave it? 👇

videos.title: How Is Pasta Made? (Rough Pasta Holds More Sauce) 🍝
videos.description:
Dry pasta is just durum wheat semolina and water. A giant screw pushes the dough through a die, and every shape has its own die. Old-school bronze dies leave the pasta rough so the sauce clings; non-stick dies make it smooth. Then it dries, fast in factories or slowly for up to two days.
What's your favorite pasta shape? 👇

videos.title: How Is Toothpaste Made? (Tubes Are Filled From the Bottom) 🪥
videos.description:
Fine chalk, fluoride, glycerin, a bit of foam and mint, mixed inside a vacuum so no air bubbles get trapped. Empty tubes stand cap-down and are filled through the open bottom, then squashed, sealed and stamped. Striped toothpaste? The colors wait near the tip and come out together with the white.
Do you squeeze from the middle? 👇
